data.one_liner: package:video_player implementation for all platforms powered by package:media_kit.
data.what_it_does: Allows standard package:video_player code to run across Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS, and Linux by using package:media_kit as the underlying backend. It provides support for more video and audio formats and codecs than the default platform implementations.
use_when: You want to use the familiar package:video_player API but need broader platform support including Windows, macOS, and Linux.
You need better video and audio codec support across platforms than the default video_player implementations provide.
avoid_when: You prefer using package:media_kit directly without the video_player abstraction layer.
You want a dedicated media player package with specialized features not exposed by video_player.
strengths: Enables package:video_player on desktop platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux) and web.
Leverages the robust media_kit backend for enhanced codec support.
Requires only a single-line initialization before normal video_player usage.
weaknesses: Requires adding platform-specific media_kit dependency libraries for full functionality.
Inherits limitations of the package:video_player API wrapper.
data.setup_notes: Add video_player_media_kit and corresponding media_kit_libs_* packages to pubspec.yaml, then call VideoPlayerMediaKit.ensureInitialized in main().

alternatives.name: video_player
alternatives.why_pick_it: The official plugin, though it may lack out-of-the-box desktop support on older versions compared to media_kit.

alternatives.name: just_audio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you primarily need feature-rich audio playback with precise control.

alternatives.name: media_kit
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want to use the native media_kit API directly rather than the video_player compatibility wrapper.
